newsitem.title: USA: Worldwide chip sales fell 0.9 pct in December.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide chip sales fell 0.9 pct in December.

text.p: Worldwide semiconductor sales fell 0.9 percent in December, reflecting only modest gains in the Americas and the Asia Pacific markets and declines in Europe and Japan, a trade group reported Friday.
According to data compiled by the Semiconductor Industry Association, worldwide chip sales fell to $10.99 billion last month from $11.09 billion in November and $13.17 billion in December of 1995.

Chip sales rose less than one percent in the Americas and Asia-Pacific markets last month, but fell two percent in Europe and Japan. For all of 1996, worlwide semiconductor billings fell 8.6 percent to $131.97 billion.
The worldwide index replaces a previous report issued by the trade group that focused only on the Americas market.

However, unlike the previous report, which measured the value of sales to orders in ratio, the new report only reveals sales information. Analysts have criticized the change because, by excluding order information, the report does not provide an indication of future demand for semiconductors.

"Chip sales remained relatively flat in December in all four markets," said Doug Andrey, director of information systems and finance for the SIA. "However, we still expect 1997 to be a growth year for the chip industry."
He said the group expects worlwide chip revenues to rise seven percent this year.

In the Americas market, December billings rose 0.2 percent to $3.53 billion, while in Asia Pacific, billings rose 0.9 percent to $2.34 billion. December billings in Europe fell 2.5 percent to $2.33 billion, while in the Japanese market, billings dropped 2.2 percent to $2.79 billion.
The group said the global report will be issued monthly.
